evidence.originalText: Connect ChatGPT to your Dock workspace using the MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector — so ChatGPT can read your data, write to your tables, update docs, and run real work from the same chat. Full 90-second walkthrough. Most people use ChatGPT alone: they ask, copy the answer, paste it somewhere else. With MCP enabled, ChatGPT becomes an actual teammate inside your workspace. This tutorial shows the exact setup using ChatGPT's Developer mode, no API keys required (OAuth handles auth automatically). ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ WHAT YOU'LL LEARN ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • How to enable Developer mode in ChatGPT (Settings → Apps → Advanced) • How to create a custom MCP connector in ChatGPT • How to add an MCP server URL (Dock example: trydock.ai/api/mcp) • How OAuth authentication works for ChatGPT MCP apps • How to verify ChatGPT can read AND write to your workspace • Same setup pattern for Claude, Cursor, Gemini, and every assistant that supports MCP ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ THE 3-STEP SETUP ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Step 1 — Sign up to Dock at https://trydock.ai (no API key needed) Step 2 — In ChatGPT: Settings → Apps → Advanced → toggle Developer mode ON Step 3 — Click Create app → Name: Dock → MCP Server URL: https://trydock.ai/api/mcp → Authentication: OAuth → tick risk box → Create After Create, OAuth runs automatically and ChatGPT gains access to all Dock tools (create_workspace, add_rows, update_doc, comments, surfaces). You can then prompt: "List my Dock workspaces", "Add a row to my tasks table", "Update the brief doc" — and ChatGPT will write directly to your Dock workspace. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ FAQ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Q: What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)? A: MCP is the open protocol from Anthropic that lets AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor connect to external tools and data sources securely. Instead of building custom integrations, any MCP-compatible AI can read from and write to any MCP server. Q: Do I need an API key to connect Dock to ChatGPT? A: No. Dock's MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 with Dynamic Client Registration. When you create the app in ChatGPT, OAuth runs automatically and grants ChatGPT scoped access to your workspaces. Q: Where is the Developer mode setting in ChatGPT? A: ChatGPT → Settings (top-right profile menu) → Apps → Advanced → Developer mode toggle. Note: Developer mode is flagged ELEVATED RISK by OpenAI because custom MCP servers can modify data. Q: What's the Dock MCP server URL? A: https://trydock.ai/api/mcp Q: Will this work with Claude, Cursor, Gemini? A: Yes. The same MCP server URL works with every AI client that supports MCP — Claude Desktop, Cursor, Gemini's tool layer, Continue.dev, and others. Q: Is Dock free? A: Yes. The free tier supports 3 agents, 6 humans, 20 workspaces, 500 rows per workspace, and 10,000 API calls per month. Sign up at trydock.ai. Q: What can ChatGPT do once connected to Dock? A: Read workspaces, list rows, create rows, update document content (markdown + mermaid + math), append doc sections, post comments, search across surfaces, list recent events. Full tool catalog at trydock.ai/docs/mcp. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ CHAPTERS ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 0:00 Intro — what if ChatGPT could do real work? 0:17 Step 1 — Sign up to Dock (no API keys, OAuth handles auth) 0:27 Step 2 — Open ChatGPT Settings → Apps → Developer mode 0:34 Step 3 — Create app, paste MCP server URL, accept risk, Create 0:46 ChatGPT now has every Dock tool (live demo) 0:57 Real work, not just answers 1:01 Works with Claude, Cursor, Gemini, every MCP-compatible AI ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ LINKS ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 🌐 Dock: https://trydock.ai 📘 Connect ChatGPT docs: https://trydock.ai/docs/connect/chatgpt 📘 MCP reference: https://trydock.ai/docs/mcp 📘 Full docs: https://trydock.ai/docs ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Dock is the AI workspace for you, your team, and every agent you run. evidence.text:
The most critical use case for leveraging the history of your desktop as context for LLMs is automated recall and workflow continuity.

Why?
Most productivity and knowledge-intensive tasks involve switching between multiple applications, searching for past information, and recalling prior interactions. An LLM with persistent desktop history can:
• Answer questions with precise context: Instantly retrieve relevant information from previous emails, Slack messages, PDFs, or documents when you ask something related.
• Auto-complete tasks with contextual memory: Fill out reports, emails, or code snippets by referencing past work, avoiding repetitive lookups.
• Reduce cognitive load: Instead of relying on human memory, the AI can surface the right data at the right time, improving decision-making.
• Detect inconsistencies and provide corrections: Identify contradictions between past and present work to flag potential mistakes.
• Automate repetitive processes: Suggest or even execute actions based on historical patterns, like summarizing meetings or drafting responses.

Most Immediate High-Impact Use Cases
Instant Recall: “What was that article I was reading yesterday about X?” or “Show me the PDF where I saw that regulation.” (e.g. open source Rewind, already launched on screenpipe, fork it and make it better)
Context-Aware Writing & Coding: Autocomplete emails, documents, or code based on previous work.
Smart Search & Recommendations: Find and suggest files, notes, or messages relevant to your current work.
Meeting & Conversation Summaries: Automatically summarize meetings or messages, incorporating past discussions.  (already on screenpipe, fork it and make it better)
Preventing Work Duplication: Detect when you’re starting to work on something you’ve already done and suggest reusing existing content.
Note-taking, productivity report: keep log of things you work on throughout the day/week/month/year, push the data to Obsidian/Notion/Linear/Jira/etc. (already on screenpipe, fork it and make it better)

evidence.originalText:
Hey everyone, we're Mathieu, Thomas and Nicolas, two brothers and a best friend building COACH.

TL;DR: We're building the best coach for in-person sales ever built: reps record every in-person meeting from our app, and our AI turns it into precise, personalized coaching. And it works so well that 5 months in, thousands of reps already run on COACH, and we're live with the top 5 in-person sales companies in France, lifting conversion rates by 32% on average.

The Problem

85% of sales in the world happen face-to-face. And in-person selling is brutally hard: a rep alone in someone's living room, reading signals, handling doubts, feeling the exact moment to push.

The best reps catch what no playbook can teach. That's why 20% of them bring in 80% of the revenue, and nobody knows what they're doing differently. The only way to find out is to physically be there: a ride-along, a full day, 100 km of driving to watch a single meeting. It doesn't scale.

The Solution

COACH's AI learns how to close customers for your business, and closes the gap at every layer of the sales org:

Every rep gets a personal coach: they record every in-person meeting from our mobile app — in-home, showroom, door-to-door — and walk out of each one with personal, precise feedback and a clear path to the next close. Our AI learns from your top 20% and coaches everyone to perform like them, starting each day with a morning brief on their weakest point. 90% improve on it in their first week.
The company gets a sales brain that learns how to close its customers: every meeting feeds it. Why is one region closing twice as much as another? Which objection is killing deals this month? Leadership just asks — COACH has the answer.
Thousands of reps already run on COACH — live with the top 5 in-person sales companies in France, where we've lifted conversion rates by 32% on average, and dozens of reps 3–4×'d their numbers. We're now growing fast in the USA, where our first customers are switching from virtual ride-along platforms to COACH.

Every rep gets a coach. Your company gets a brain.

The Team

At 18 and 21, we built Alsace Test: a 44-rep field sales team that did €3.5M in 14 months. Alsace made us fall in love with in-person sales, obsessed, actually.

And one thing was driving us crazy: same product, same material, same training, and one guy closed 4× more than the others. We were driving 2,000 km a week just to watch reps sell.

So we asked them to record themselves. Suddenly, without moving, we were listening to 10 hours of meetings a day. That was COACH before COACH.

In an AI-driven sales world, we're deeply convinced Zoom sales and call centers will soon be replaced by AI agents. Face-to-face selling will be the last human job on Earth. We're betting on it.

evidence.originalText: (YC S26) builds modular reactors that destroy contaminants in chip fabs, keeping wafers clean without a cleanroom. Chip features keep getting smaller, but cleanroom infrastructure does not scale with them. Semiconductor manufacturers spend billions building and operating enormous cleanrooms, then spend even more isolating their most advanced wafers from the surrounding environment. At leading-edge nodes, trace airborne contaminants can create defects, reduce yield, and disrupt some of the most sensitive manufacturing processes on Earth. But the whole factory does not need to be a cleanroom. Only the environment immediately surrounding the wafer does. The Aerogen Systems’ purification unit, Talos, integrates directly into semiconductor equipment and continuously destroys airborne molecular contaminants before they reach the wafer. Instead of relying on constant ultra-high-purity nitrogen purge and disposable filtration, Talos continuously purifies the environment inside the tool. Aerogen Systems creates 10–100x cleaner tool environments with dramatically lower dependence on purge gas. Talos is the foundation for the Aerogen Systems Cleanpipe, an ultra-clean infrastructure that connects semiconductor tools and protects wafers as they move across the fab. Aerogen Systems began as a NASA-funded research group at the University of Michigan, combining CEO Noah Vogel’s experience improving manufacturing rate and yield at SpaceX with CTO Colin Lavery’s background in particle detection and destruction. Together, they’re applying those disciplines to semiconductor fabs, where eliminating microscopic contaminants can directly improve throughput, manufacturing economics, and chip yield. There are certain limits here: the benchmark mixes cell-type, perturbation, and context shift, so we cannot cleanly assign the gap to one axis of generalization.

evidence.text: When was the last time you actually verified that a piece of software does what it claims? Not read the terms of service. Not taken a vendor's word for it. Actually verified it. For most organizations, including most security teams, the answer is never. We've built the digital economy on delegation. You sign contracts. You buy insurance. The shift happening now is fundamental: from "trust us" to "verify it yourself." Verifiable compute makes that technically possible
evidence.originalText:
When was the last time you actually verified that a piece of software does what it claims?

Not read the terms of service.
Not taken a vendor's word for it.
Actually verified it.

For most organizations, including most security teams, the answer is never.
We've built the digital economy on delegation. You sign contracts. You buy insurance. You trust that vendors are telling the truth about how your data is handled.

That works until it doesn't. And it often doesn't.

The shift happening now is fundamental: from "trust us" to "verify it yourself." Verifiable compute makes that technically possible for the first time.

evidence.originalText:
Everyone owns skincare products, but nobody knows what's actually working.

Your skin reacts to everything in your daily life: your sleep, stress, water, products, even the humidity in the air. Nothing has ever captured any of it.

The Lumoscope is a multispectral camera that clips onto your phone and scans your skin at home with the same light used in clinics. You see what a mirror can't: a breakout days before it surfaces, and sun damage years before it shows. Every scan is scored on hydration, redness, evenness, pigmentation, texture, and pores, and it compounds into a record of your own skin, so you can finally tell whether the serum you started in March is doing anything.

Lumi, the skin coach in the app, reads that history, connects flare-ups to causes you'd never suspect, and matches products from 18,000+ options to your data instead of a population average, so you finally know what works for you, and can track those records over time.

Lumeria is patent pending, built off 150+ derm and patient interviews, 2 clinical partnerships, and is YC backed.

Preorders are open at the $199 founding price until August 16, then only goes up. Ships Sep–Oct 2026.

Link in bio. 💛

evidence.originalText:
Pacific (YC S26) mass-produces and deploys micro data centers for Earth and space, faster than anyone else.

New data centers wait years for grid connections, meanwhile, delayed construction projects across America sit on live, unused interconnects, losing $1B a week in interest on debt. The power is built and paid for but unused; so we turn it into an AI factory. Our first two sites go live this month with a factory to follow and $105M in future delivery contracts.

Pacific's pods land on those sites and generate revenue within days. Diamond wafers in the cooling system let them run anywhere on Earth, even a desert, without evaporating water - and eventually in space. Each pod is a standardized, movable asset backed by take-or-pay contracts, meaning we finance it like an aircraft - debt at 5–-6%, not 11-15%. Pods cost us nothing to build; lenders fund them and the contracts pay them back.

SpaceX didn't just build rockets, they built rocket factories - we're doing the same for data centers. Pacific vertically integrates the components that carry multi-year lead times - transformers, switchgear, and power distribution - to fill the $11 trillion of demand for compute infrastructure this decade.

The team is led by a second-time founder and spans ex-Google engineering, JP Morgan AI, Cambridge computer science.

If you are compute constrained or need a secure cluster, talk to us here: 

Join pacific as we build supercomputers for the galaxy!

Congratulations Harper and the team!

evidence.originalText:
Understudy cuts companies’ Anthropic bills by up to 80% without sacrificing performance.

Companies spend millions renting general-purpose frontier models, but almost none of that spending compounds. Every prompt generates useful experience, yet turning production traces into evaluations, training data, and specialized models normally requires an entire ML team.

Understudy automates that process. It observes AI workloads, builds evaluations, trains smaller open-weight models, and deploys them only when they outperform the incumbent on quality, cost, and latency. Customers own the resulting models and can run them in Understudy’s cloud, their own cloud, or on-premise. Founders Luis and Aamir previously built optimization and experimentation systems at Instacart that helped scale multiple business lines beyond $1B in annual revenue.

evidence.authorName: screenpipe
evidence.title: OpenAI's Privacy Filter + Hardware Enclave + screenpipe =  truly private screen AI
evidence.text:
Screenpipe captures everything you see, say, and hear on your computer.

But what happens to that data when AI analyzes it? Until now: it had to leave your machine to a cloud AI provider that could technically see it.

Today that changes.

We're integrating OpenAI's new Privacy Filter (released April 2026) and running it inside a NVIDIA H200 confidential-compute enclave. Here's what that means in plain English:

→ Your screen data leaves your computer encrypted
→ It enters a hardware enclave that nobody — not even us — can see into
→ The Privacy Filter model strips names, addresses, emails, phone numbers, URLs, dates, account numbers, and secrets
→ The redacted data comes back to your computer, still encrypted end-to-end
→ Your AI can now work on the cleaned data without ever exposing the raw version

No trust required. No "we promise we don't look." Hardware-enforced privacy.

Available today in Screenpipe chat and pipes.

Download Screenpipe → https://screenpi.pe/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=[redacted-public-param]&utm_content=description

—

Learn more:
• OpenAI Privacy Filter — https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-privacy-filter/
• Screenpipe security architecture — https://screenpi.pe/security
• Screenpipe SDK (for embedders) — https://screenpi.pe/sdk

Follow along:
• X / Twitter — https://twitter.com/screen_pipe
• GitHub — https://github.com/screenpipe/screenpipe
• Discord — https://discord.gg/screenpipe

evidence.originalText:
HyperProbe lets your coding agent debug production by reading the actual variable values on the failing line, without adding a log or redeploying.

When code breaks in prod and the value you need was never logged, your agent is stuck guessing from logs. HyperProbe lets it drop a read-only probe on the exact line in your running service, capture the real state when live traffic hits it, and diagnose from evidence instead of inference.

Try it: hyperprobe.co

What it does:

Your agent places a probe on one line in the live service, over MCP
It captures the local variables and call stack the next time real traffic hits that line
No redeploy, no restart, nothing pauses
Read-only. Redaction happens in-process, before anything leaves your container
Self-host option so no captured state leaves your network
Supports Node, Java, and Python

The bugs this is for are the quiet ones. A call times out and returns null, null gets read as zero, a user sees a wrong balance. An upstream API starts returning a number as a string. None of them throw, most return 200, and the value that explains them was never written down. Those are the incidents that eat an afternoon and often get filed as a known quirk.

Built by Shailendra and Karan. Backed by Y Combinator.

evidence.title: Connect Your Screen to n8n — AI Automation Based on What You  Actually Do
evidence.text:
Your screen activity can now trigger n8n workflows automatically.

In this video I show how to connect screenpipe (open source screen + audio capture) to n8n so AI watches what you're working on and triggers automations - no manual input needed.

Examples:
- Detect you're in a meeting → auto-generate summary in Notion
- See you're researching a topic → save links + notes to your knowledge base
- Notice a Slack message about a bug → create a Linear issue

screenpipe captures everything on your screen locally, pipes process it with AI, and n8n handles the workflow logic.

evidence.authorName: screenpipe
evidence.title: screenpipe v482: Accessibility Tree, Smarter AI  Chat, Everything Faster
evidence.text:
Screenpipe v0.482 — biggest update in weeks.

What's new:
→ Accessibility tree walker: reads UI elements directly from your OS instead of OCR. Way less CPU, way more accurate text extraction.
→ Smarter AI chat: powered by a coding agent (same tech behind Claude Code). Works great with local models (Ollama, Qwen).
→ UI events: keyboard input, clipboard, clicks — all captured and searchable on the timeline.
→ 2-second search across everything you've seen and heard.
→ Voice training for speaker identification.
→ Way fewer crashes, faster everything.

How to enable accessibility tree: Settings → Screen → enable "Accessibility" text extraction.

Everything runs locally. Open source.

Download: https://screenpi.pe?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=v482-update
GitHub: https://github.com/screenpipe/screenpipe

#screenpipe #ai #opensource #productivity #screenrecording

what is it?
i often find myself answering the same type of questions over and over again, but nobody else can do that for me since i hold the context of the conversation/project/life. well, until now. new screenpipe feature allows you to generate contextualized replies with a simple shortcut in 3 seconds

evidence.authorName: screenpipe
evidence.title: screenpipe talk at south park commons - AI powered by   everything you've seen, said, or heard
evidence.text:
screenpipe at south park commons — the technical briefing.

how we built local-first AI memory that captures, indexes, and acts on everything you see, say, and hear — without sending it to the cloud.

→ watch the slides: https://screenpi.pe/talks/south-park-commons?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=spc-talk
→ try it (mac · windows · linux): https://screenpi.pe/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=spc-talk
→ source (MIT, 18.5K ★): https://github.com/screenpipe/screenpipe
→ we're hiring (eng · applied AI · enterprise BD)

what's covered:
• the gap — your screen has the context, your AI doesn't
• architecture — three layers, all on-device
• rewind, ask, search, pipes — the four product surfaces
• data model — sqlite at ~/.screenpipe/db.sqlite
• local API on :3030 — the agent surface
• agent runtime — how a pipe runs (BYOK, BYO runtime, observable)
• why local-first — the line cloud-recall competitors can't cross
• enterprise stack — license, fleet policy, signed builds
• where we are — 250K+ installs, design partners, what's next



— louis
@louis030195 · louis@screenpi.pe

evidence.text:
I don't think many people realize how powerful claude can be with /goal

Tried asking it a weird prompt to see what it would do: 
/goal make a baked smoothie

Initially, it correctly reasoned that smoothies are blended, not baked, and made some ascii art and ingredients for the smoothie. When claude declared itself done, /goal told claude that it had not met its goal; the user asked for a baked smoothie, not a blended one.

It ended up redoing the ascii into the shape of a baked potato and adjusted the instructions accordingly

The lesson: 
Use /goal responsibly

evidence.title: scraping you desktop content in milliseconds to feed AI context window
evidence.text:

this feature allows you to instantly pass the data content to any downstream application, such as an AI chatbot that can help you ask more personalized questions, get more relevant insights, find information you browsed, and more.

open source: https://github.com/mediar-ai/screenpipe
download app: https://screenpi.pe"

evidence.title: Recalled the perfect valentine's day spot in 3 seconds flat

screenpipe records your screen 24/7, locally, and lets you search anything you've ever seen, said or heard.
